test_title: PYST 3: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - GA (Held On 26 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following best explains the origin of eskers in glaciated landscapes?

options.text: Ridges carved by ice cutting bedrock
Sinuous ridges from subglacial meltwater deposition
Hills shaped by ice pushing sediments

solution:
The correct answer is __**Sinuous ridges from subglacial meltwater deposition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eskers** are prominent **fluvio-glacial landforms** characterized by long, narrow, and **sinuous ridges** of **stratified drift**, primarily consisting of **sand and gravel**.
 
• The origin of these structures is attributed to **meltwater streams** flowing through **subglacial tunnels** (beneath the ice) or **englacial channels** (within the ice) under high hydrostatic pressure.
 
• As the **glacier** becomes stagnant and begins to melt, the velocity of the internal stream decreases, causing the **deposition of sediments** along the floor of the ice tunnel.
 
• Once the surrounding **glacial ice** completely disappears, the accumulated sediment is left behind as a **continuous ridge** that winds across the landscape, often reaching heights of several meters and lengths of many kilometers.
 
• Unlike landforms created directly by ice, the materials in an **esker** are **sorted and layered** because they were transported and deposited by **flowing water**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glacial Till and Moraines**:

 
 
• **Moraines** are ridges formed from **till**, which is **unsorted sediment** deposited directly by the ice rather than meltwater.
 
• **Terminal moraines** mark the furthest reach of a glacier, while **lateral moraines** form along the sides of the **glacial valley**.
 
 
 
• **Drumlins**:
 
 
• These are **oval-shaped or teardrop-shaped hills** formed by the **streamlining** of till or **sediment deformation** under the weight of a moving glacier.
 
• The **steep side** of a drumlin faces the direction from which the **ice advanced**, while the tapered tail points in the direction of **ice flow**.
 
 
 
• **Erosional Landforms**:
 
 
• Landforms like **U-shaped valleys**, **fjords**, and **cirques** are created by the **erosive action** of ice cutting into the **bedrock**, contrasting with the **depositional nature** of eskers.
